name: Subset sums strictly increase along inclusion; no proper subset sum divides the total

insights: Erdős #882: largest A ⊆ {1,…,n} whose non-empty subset sums are pairwise non-dividing (answer (1+o(1))log₂ n). Sibling oq-03 proves ValidSubset is downward closed (subset-lattice direction); sibling oq-03-oq-01 proves a valid set is an antichain under divisibility and (for |A|≥2) no single element divides ∑A. This child works the orthogonal CHAIN direction of the subset lattice.

Pivot = strict monotonicity of the summing map S ↦ ∑S along strict inclusions. For S ⊊ T ⊆ A the witnessing element of T∖S is positive (validity gives 1 ≤ a), so Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_subset yields ∑S < ∑T (subsetSum_lt_of_ssubset). Hence the two subset sums are distinct.

Headline subsetSum_not_dvd_of_ssubset: for a valid A and a strict chain ∅ ≠ S ⊊ T ⊆ A, neither ∑S nor ∑T divides the other — distinctness (from strict monotonicity) feeds the divisibility-free hypothesis on subsetSums A.

Headline proper_subset_not_dvd_total: NO proper non-empty subset sum divides the total ∑A. Specialising T = A. Taking S = {a} recovers the sibling's per-element result (elem_not_dvd_total), so 'no element divides the total' is exactly the singleton case of a uniform chain phenomenon.

Geometric picture: along every chain in the subset lattice of a feasible set the sums form a strictly increasing sequence that is simultaneously pairwise non-dividing — a strict chain in value that is an antichain in divisibility.
builtItems: Erdos882ProblemOQ03OQ02.lean: 4 defs + 6 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, self-contained (re-declares nonemptySubsets/subsetSums/DivisibilityFree/ValidSubset on modern Finset API).

subsetSum_mem (general membership ∑S ∈ subsetSums A for ∅≠S⊆A), subsetSum_lt_of_ssubset (S⊊T⊆A ⟹ ∑S<∑T via Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_subset + Finset.exists_of_ssubset), subsetSum_lt_total (proper subset sum < total).

subsetSum_not_dvd_of_ssubset (chain: neither sum divides the other), proper_subset_not_dvd_total (no proper subset sum divides ∑A), elem_not_dvd_total (singleton case recovering the sibling's headline via Finset.ssubset_iff_of_subset + exists_mem_ne).
knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE. Child of erdos-882-oq-03 (structural theory). Where oq-03 proves downward closure and oq-03-oq-01 proves A is a divisibility antichain, this entry exposes the CHAIN structure: the summing map is strictly monotone along strict subset inclusions, so subset sums of a strictly nested pair are distinct and (with the divisibility-free hypothesis) pairwise non-dividing. Headline proper_subset_not_dvd_total — no proper non-empty subset sum divides the total — uniformly strengthens the sibling's per-element statement, which is recovered as the singleton case (elem_not_dvd_total). All 0-axiom verified (#print axioms = propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only), no native_decide. Self-contained.
nextSteps: Strengthen distinctness: prove subset sums are injective on any chain in the lattice, then count chains to connect with the (1+o(1))log₂ n cardinality answer.
Disjoint version: for disjoint nonempty S,T ⊆ A with distinct sums the divisibility-free condition still applies — formalize the disjoint analogue (distinctness is the only extra hypothesis needed).
Quantify: bound the length of a strictly increasing pairwise-non-dividing chain of subset sums inside {1,…,n·|A|}, linking the chain picture to the extremal cardinality.
